facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: the 10-K and the three quarterly reports give audited annual and unaudited quarterly statements through June 30, 2026, with the debt notes, a facility-by-facility warehouse table (page:14), a senior note table (page:17), a liquidity discussion (page:48 to page:60) and a subsequent-event note (page:31 to page:33). The Q2 release addendum adds five quarters of balance sheet and operations (page:8 to page:12). - Strongest contrary evidence: the subsequent-event note says the August 5, 2026 raise "closed subsequent to June 30, 2026" and that "the effects of the transaction have not been reflected" in the statements (page:33). facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: UWM Holdings Corp is a wholesale mortgage originator whose reported debt has two parts that must be read separately: warehouse lines of 8,600.1 million that finance mortgage loans for days or weeks, and non-funding debt of 6,040.4 million (senior notes, servicing-rights facilities, borrowings against investment securities and finance leases) that finances the corporate balance sheet and the 5,311.5 million servicing-rights asset. The company's own leverage measure is non-funding debt to total equity, which was 6.13x at June 30, 2026 against 2.69x at December 31, 2025, because debt rose by 1,747.5 million while total equity fell by 608.3 million to 985.3 million. On Adjusted EBITDA, which already deducts warehouse interest but not interest on non-funding debt, non-funding debt was 7.64x the last twelve months at June 30, 2026 (790.6 million), against 6.16x at FY2025 (697.3 million). Earnings quality is the central issue: Adjusted EBITDA for Q2 2026 was 185.9 million while the net loss was 451.9 million, because the company adds back a 603.2 million loss on other interest rate derivatives and removes a 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain. For the last twelve months those two excluded items net to a 526.8 million loss, and net loss was 105.0 million. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: UWM Holdings Corp is the listed top holding company of a wholesale-only residential mortgage lender, so its creditors are exposed to one volume-driven business that earns through gain on sale, a retained servicing portfolio and net interest, and that is controlled by a single holder. The operating subsidiary originates only through independent mortgage brokers, sells about 93% of loans into Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae pools, and keeps the servicing rights on most of them, which is why the servicing-rights asset of 5,311.5 million and the borrowings against it dominate the funding story. Control rests with SFS Corp., an entity controlled by the CEO: it holds 78.7% of the economic units of Holdings LLC and, as the 10-K states, about 79% of voting power, and it is also the lender under the unsecured revolver, the counterparty to the Tax Receivable Agreement, and the recipient of member distributions. The decisive recent changes are two. First, the planned acquisition of Two Harbors Investment Corp., signed on December 17, 2025 and described in the 10-K as expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, was terminated in the first quarter of 2026 with a termination fee received, so the share issuance of roughly 247 million Class A shares and the added servicing portfolio did not occur. Second, on August 5, 2026, after a second quarter in which derivative losses drove a net loss of 451.9 million, the company closed a 1.65 billion preferred stock and warrant issue to Oaktree and a vehicle of the CEO's family, suspended the quarterly dividend, and announced a contingent 400 million rights offering. These actions add junior capital beneath the debt, but the filings supplied describe the preferred terms only in summary, and the effects are not in any reported financial statement. A creditor should therefore treat the capital raise as a material, documented positive for liquidity and loss absorption whose strength depends on terms that are not in the pack, while keeping the controlled-company structure, related-party flows and the in-house servicing transition as the main governance and execution uncertainties.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On August 5, 2026 UWMC closed a "strategic capital transaction" with affiliates of Oaktree Capital Management and entities affiliated with its Chairman, President and CEO, with gross proceeds of 1.65 billion (Q2 10-Q page:32). Oaktree invested 1.5 billion for 1.5 million shares of Series A-1 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 150 million Class A shares at 2.00 per share and over 150 million at 6.00 per share. SFS Group Capital, LLC invested 150.0 million for 150,000 shares of Series A-2 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 15 million shares at 2.00 and over 15 million at 6.00. Both series have an original issue price of 1,000 per share and accrue cumulative dividends of 10.0% per annum when paid in cash or 13.0% per annum when not paid in cash and added to stated value. Series A-2 is subordinate to Series A-1 in certain circumstances and has no governance protections. The certificate of designation includes redemption, governance and investor-protection rights for Series A-1 holders that the note does not describe, and an investor rights agreement lets Oaktree appoint two directors, one of them independent. In connection with the issue the company announced its intention to launch a 400 million rights offering to Class A holders "if needed", with the support of Oaktree and the Ishbia family, at a price equal to the greater of 2.00 and 85% of a ten-day volume-weighted average price, for up to 200 million Class A shares, with a record date of October 2, 2026 and expiry on November 12, 2026 (page:33). The filing states the effects are not reflected in the financial statements. The Q2 release headline calls the transaction a "$2.05 Billion Equity Investment"; the filing treats the 1.65 billion as closed and the 400 million as contingent, and the two are logged as a conflict below. Use of proceeds, issuance costs, balance sheet classification (equity or mezzanine), the redemption terms and the financing effect on the servicing-rights facilities are Insufficient Information. This is an equity-type transaction; it adds no new debt.

facts.text: New debt issues in the period covered: the most recent senior note issue was the 1.0 billion 6.250% senior notes due March 15, 2031 issued on September 9, 2025 by Holdings LLC and guaranteed by UWM; its proceeds were used to repay the 800.0 million 2025 senior notes at maturity, temporarily pay down servicing-rights facilities and for working capital (Q2 10-Q page:17 to page:18, page:53). Debt capacity rose through facility changes: the Ginnie Mae servicing-rights facility was amended in March 2026 to 900.0 million of uncommitted capacity with later maturity, and by June 30, 2026 the two servicing-rights facilities show limits of 2.0 billion and 1.25 billion (Q1 10-Q page:16; Q2 10-Q page:15 to page:16); the amendment that raised those limits in the second quarter is not described. Drawn balances on the servicing-rights lines were 2,950.0 million at June 30, 2026 against 1,200.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: UWM Holdings Corp is a large, agency-focused mortgage originator whose credit position weakened in the first half of 2026 but was cushioned by new capital on August 5, 2026. The strongest support is the USD 1,650.0 million preferred issue, together with scale in agency-eligible origination and a USD 5,311.5 million servicing-rights asset. The weakest point is the balance sheet: non-funding debt of USD 6,040.4 million is 6.13x total equity of USD 985.3 million, and equity fell USD 615.6 million in the second quarter, mostly from a net loss driven by derivative losses. What decides the outcome is whether the preferred terms leave creditors protected, whether the uncommitted servicing-rights lines stay available into USD 2,375.0 million of 2027 maturities, and whether hedging losses stop.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Leverage on the company's own capital measure more than doubled in six months. Non-funding debt (senior notes, servicing-rights lines, borrowings against investment securities and finance leases) rose by USD 1,747.5 million, from USD 4,292.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 6,040.4 million at June 30, 2026, while total equity fell by USD 608.3 million, from USD 1,593.6 million to USD 985.3 million, taking non-funding debt to equity from 2.69x to 6.13x [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]. The increase was USD 1,750.0 million of net draws on the two servicing-rights facilities, which exceeded the USD 1,237.7 million growth in the servicing-rights asset, so part of the borrowing financed operations and distributions rather than the asset. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the use of proceeds.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 2. Adjusted EBITDA and net income diverged sharply because of hedging. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months was USD 790.6 million, and non-funding debt was 7.64x that figure, against 6.16x at FY2025; yet the last twelve months produced a net loss of USD 105.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA excludes servicing-rights valuation changes and the result on other interest rate derivatives, which together were a net loss of USD 526.8 million over the last twelve months and USD 538.1 million in the second quarter alone. In the second quarter a derivative loss of USD 603.2 million was only partly offset by a USD 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain, so the hedge programme lost money net. The filings do not state the intended hedge ratio. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the hedge result.

- Uncommitted and short-dated funding with cross-default. Only USD 900.0 million of warehouse line capacity is committed, the servicing-rights facilities are uncommitted and collateral-based, and cross-default links all lines [Q2 10-Q `page:15`, `page:52`]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Controlling-holder claims and related-party flows. Tax Receivable Agreement liability of USD 280.0 million, member distributions of USD 261.9 million paid in the first half of 2026, and related-party payments of USD 32.9 million in FY2025 [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour; Claims outside debt in CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Execution and legal risks. The in-house servicing transition (management targets October 2026) and class actions on broker influence, telemarketing and a vendor cyber incident; no accrual or estimate is printed [CP-1A, Timeline; Credit translations]. Category: Management Language for the timeline; Documentary Fact for the proceedings.

- Terms of the August 2026 raise are unknown. Redemption and protective rights of the Series A-1 preferred and the board rights of Oaktree could rank ahead of creditor interests in practice. The filing does not say. Category: Insufficient Information.

### Financial base view

UWM Holdings Corp is a wholesale mortgage originator whose reported debt has two parts that must be read separately: warehouse lines of 8,600.1 million that finance mortgage loans for days or weeks, and non-funding debt of 6,040.4 million (senior notes, servicing-rights facilities, borrowings against investment securities and finance leases) that finances the corporate balance sheet and the 5,311.5 million servicing-rights asset. The company's own leverage measure is non-funding debt to total equity, which was 6.13x at June 30, 2026 against 2.69x at December 31, 2025, because debt rose by 1,747.5 million while total equity fell by 608.3 million to 985.3 million. On Adjusted EBITDA, which already deducts warehouse interest but not interest on non-funding debt, non-funding debt was 7.64x the last twelve months at June 30, 2026 (790.6 million), against 6.16x at FY2025 (697.3 million). Earnings quality is the central issue: Adjusted EBITDA for Q2 2026 was 185.9 million while the net loss was 451.9 million, because the company adds back a 603.2 million loss on other interest rate derivatives and removes a 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain. For the last twelve months those two excluded items net to a 526.8 million loss, and net loss was 105.0 million. Operating cash flow was negative 1,885.8 million for H1 2026, with servicing-rights sale proceeds of 801.0 million in investing activities, and the gap was funded by 1,750.0 million of net borrowing on the servicing-rights lines. Liquidity on the company's basis is about 1.3 billion (1,298.4 million with restricted cash), but 300.0 million of the undrawn lines is uncommitted and the 500.0 million revolver is provided by SFS Corp., an entity controlled by the CEO. Cash of 321.8 million was paid to equity holders in H1 2026 through dividends and member distributions. Warehouse lines with 5,090.8 million advanced expire on or before May 14, 2027, and 2,375.0 million of non-funding debt (the 2027 notes and the Conventional servicing-rights facility) falls due in 2027. All figures are unaudited for 2026 and exclude the August 5, 2026 preferred stock and warrant transaction, which closed after the period.

### Earnings, cash flow and servicing drivers

- Revenue: Q2 2026 total revenue of 888,003 was 17.0% above Q2 2025 (758,700) and 1.5% below Q1 2026 (901,427). H1 2026 revenue of 1,789,430 was 30.4% above H1 2025. Volume was flat year on year in Q2 (39.7 billion against 39.7 billion) and up 17.4% for the half (84.6 billion against 72.1 billion; Q2 10-Q `page:37`); the revenue gain came from gain margin (1.33% in Q2 2026 against 1.13% in Q2 2025) and servicing income (220,503 against 178,813).

- Expenses: H1 2026 total expenses of 1,210,444 rose 19.6% from 1,012,366; Q2 2026 general and administrative expense of 89,748 rose from 59,999, which the filing attributes to software licensing, legal fees and costs of the terminated Two Harbors merger (`page:46`).

- Net loss: the Q2 2026 net loss of 451,902 compares with net income of 314,479 in Q2 2025, a swing of 766,381, with other gains (losses), net moving from a gain of 97,483 to a loss of 725,874 (`page:3`, `page:47`).

- Servicing-rights asset: fair value rose from 4,073,781 to 5,311,465 over six months (up 1,237,684) on capitalization of 2,142,855, sales of 822,996, valuation-input gains of 312,953 and decay of 395,128 (`page:12`). Fair value is 2.14% of the 247,648,881 unpaid principal balance serviced, against 1.69% at December 31, 2025. Weighted average discount rate fell to 8.9% from 9.4% and weighted average prepayment speed to 8.6% from 10.3% (`page:13`). A 10% adverse change in discount rate lowers value by 207,202 and in prepayment speed by 200,467 (`page:13` to `page:14`). Loan servicing delinquency (60+ days) was 1.38% against 1.62% (`page:42`).

- Interest-rate sensitivity (company, hypothetical, June 30, 2026): a 25 basis point parallel fall lowers servicing rights by 313,118 and raises mortgage loans, interest rate lock commitments and other derivatives; a rise adds 234,587 to servicing rights and lowers the others (`page:66`). Other interest rate derivatives had a notional of 12,805,000 and fair value of 42,077 (`page:11`), and the company states it exited a significant number of positions entered at the end of Q1 2026 and in Q2 2026 (`page:60`).

- Cash flow quality: operating cash flow is distorted by origination and servicing mechanics. In H1 2026 the largest items were the non-cash capitalization of servicing rights (2,142,855 deducted), a decrease in mortgage loans at fair value (313,653 added) and the net loss (281,528). Servicing-rights sale proceeds of 801,013 sit in investing activities (`page:4` to `page:5`). The filing does not break out cash settled on derivative positions.

- Funding of the gap: financing activities provided 1,106,791 in H1 2026, including 3,650,000 borrowed and 1,900,000 repaid on secured lines (net 1,750,000) and net repayments of 312,417 on warehouse lines, after 59,867 of dividends and 261,896 of member distributions (`page:5`).

- Capital return: Class A dividends declared for H1 2026 were 65,589 and member distributions declared were 255,922 (`page:4`); the quarterly dividend was suspended after June 30, 2026 (Q2 release `page:3`). The release does not say whether the proportional distribution to SFS Corp. is also suspended; tax distributions remain required (`page:48`).

## Findings
### Reader summary

| Management says substantially all loans will be serviced in-house by October 2026; the 10-K says one sub-servicer services the portfolio. | Servicing transition is an execution and compliance risk on a 5,311.5 million asset. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

UWM Holdings Corp is the listed top holding company of a wholesale-only residential mortgage lender, so its creditors are exposed to one volume-driven business that earns through gain on sale, a retained servicing portfolio and net interest, and that is controlled by a single holder. The operating subsidiary originates only through independent mortgage brokers, sells about 93% of loans into Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae pools, and keeps the servicing rights on most of them, which is why the servicing-rights asset of 5,311.5 million and the borrowings against it dominate the funding story. Control rests with SFS Corp., an entity controlled by the CEO: it holds 78.7% of the economic units of Holdings LLC and, as the 10-K states, about 79% of voting power, and it is also the lender under the unsecured revolver, the counterparty to the Tax Receivable Agreement, and the recipient of member distributions. The decisive recent changes are two. First, the planned acquisition of Two Harbors Investment Corp., signed on December 17, 2025 and described in the 10-K as expected to close in the second quarter of 2026, was terminated in the first quarter of 2026 with a termination fee received, so the share issuance of roughly 247 million Class A shares and the added servicing portfolio did not occur. Second, on August 5, 2026, after a second quarter in which derivative losses drove a net loss of 451.9 million, the company closed a 1.65 billion preferred stock and warrant issue to Oaktree and a vehicle of the CEO's family, suspended the quarterly dividend, and announced a contingent 400 million rights offering. These actions add junior capital beneath the debt, but the filings supplied describe the preferred terms only in summary, and the effects are not in any reported financial statement. A creditor should therefore treat the capital raise as a material, documented positive for liquidity and loss absorption whose strength depends on terms that are not in the pack, while keeping the controlled-company structure, related-party flows and the in-house servicing transition as the main governance and execution uncertainties.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On August 5, 2026 UWMC closed a "strategic capital transaction" with affiliates of Oaktree Capital Management and entities affiliated with its Chairman, President and CEO, with gross proceeds of 1.65 billion (Q2 10-Q `page:32`). Oaktree invested 1.5 billion for 1.5 million shares of Series A-1 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 150 million Class A shares at 2.00 per share and over 150 million at 6.00 per share. SFS Group Capital, LLC invested 150.0 million for 150,000 shares of Series A-2 Preferred Stock plus warrants over 15 million shares at 2.00 and over 15 million at 6.00. Both series have an original issue price of 1,000 per share and accrue cumulative dividends of 10.0% per annum when paid in cash or 13.0% per annum when not paid in cash and added to stated value. Series A-2 is subordinate to Series A-1 in certain circumstances and has no governance protections. The certificate of designation includes redemption, governance and investor-protection rights for Series A-1 holders that the note does not describe, and an investor rights agreement lets Oaktree appoint two directors, one of them independent. In connection with the issue the company announced its intention to launch a 400 million rights offering to Class A holders "if needed", with the support of Oaktree and the Ishbia family, at a price equal to the greater of 2.00 and 85% of a ten-day volume-weighted average price, for up to 200 million Class A shares, with a record date of October 2, 2026 and expiry on November 12, 2026 (`page:33`). The filing states the effects are not reflected in the financial statements. The Q2 release headline calls the transaction a "$2.05 Billion Equity Investment"; the filing treats the 1.65 billion as closed and the 400 million as contingent, and the two are logged as a conflict below. Use of proceeds, issuance costs, balance sheet classification (equity or mezzanine), the redemption terms and the financing effect on the servicing-rights facilities are Insufficient Information. This is an equity-type transaction; it adds no new debt.

New debt issues in the period covered: the most recent senior note issue was the 1.0 billion 6.250% senior notes due March 15, 2031 issued on September 9, 2025 by Holdings LLC and guaranteed by UWM; its proceeds were used to repay the 800.0 million 2025 senior notes at maturity, temporarily pay down servicing-rights facilities and for working capital (Q2 10-Q `page:17` to `page:18`, `page:53`). Before that, 800.0 million of 6.625% notes due February 1, 2030 were issued by Holdings LLC on December 10, 2024. No senior notes were issued in the first half of 2026 (cash flow statement `page:5`). Debt capacity rose through facility changes: the Ginnie Mae servicing-rights facility was amended in March 2026 to 900.0 million of uncommitted capacity with later maturity, and by June 30, 2026 the two servicing-rights facilities show limits of 2.0 billion and 1.25 billion (Q1 10-Q `page:16`; Q2 10-Q `page:15` to `page:16`); the amendment that raised those limits in the second quarter is not described. Drawn balances on the servicing-rights lines were 2,950.0 million at June 30, 2026 against 1,200.0 million at December 31, 2025 (CP-1).

The terminated Two Harbors transaction: under the Merger Agreement dated December 17, 2025, Two Harbors common stockholders would receive 2.3328 UWMC Class A shares per share, and each series of Two Harbors preferred stock would convert into a like UWMC preferred series (8.125% Series A, 7.625% Series B and 7.25% Series C), with closing expected in the second quarter of 2026 (10-K `page:140`). The 10-K expected about 247 million Class A shares to be issued (`page:74`). The deck described the transaction as adding servicing UPB and being accretive and "de-levering" (management claims, deck `page:7`). The agreement was later terminated, with a fee received in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 10-Q `page:37`), and second-quarter general and administrative expense included costs "related to the terminated merger agreement" (Q2 10-Q `page:46`). Termination date, payer, fee amount and reason are Insufficient Information.

| Cash conversion and funding | Capitalized servicing rights are non-cash revenue; secured borrowings against servicing rights rose to 2,950.0 million (CP-1); facilities are uncommitted (Q2 10-Q `page:15` to `page:16`) | Production income converts to cash only when servicing is sold or collected; a lender can limit advances on uncommitted lines | Liquidity depends on lender discretion and servicing-rights values; the August 2026 raise adds a buffer | The company states a belief that cash and sources are sufficient for twelve months (Q2 10-Q `page:49`) |

| Control and sponsor alignment | SFS Corp. controls about 79% of votes, lends the revolver, receives member distributions and the Tax Receivable Agreement payments (10-K `page:73`, `page:71`) | Owner interests can differ from creditors on distributions and on change of control, where Tax Receivable Agreement payments accelerate | Neutral or Mixed; the subordinated revolver and owner-side preferred participation are the supportive facts | Dividend suspension and subordination reduce extraction risk |

| Hybrid capital | 1.65 billion Series A-1 and A-2 preferred with 10.0% cash or 13.0% non-cash dividends, warrants over 330 million shares and board rights for Oaktree (Q2 10-Q `page:32`) | Cumulative dividends and redemption rights create a fixed claim junior to debt; warrants dilute common | Positive for loss absorption if redemption cannot be forced ahead of debt; terms not supplied, so monitoring posture is to obtain the certificate of designation | Press release headline of 2.05 billion differs from the filing split |

| Servicing transition | In-house servicing expected by October 2026 (Q1 release `page:2`); one sub-servicer (10-K `page:17`) | Compliance, systems and agency-approval risks on a 247.6 billion portfolio | Execution risk to servicing income and to servicing-rights value | Management says the transition is ahead of schedule (Management Language) |

| Legal and conduct | Class actions on broker influence, telemarketing and a vendor cyber incident; a contract suit by Rocket Mortgage (Q2 10-Q `page:69` to `page:71`) | Potential damages, injunctive relief and cost; no accrual or estimate is printed | Not currently expected to be material by the company; amounts unknown | Company statement of no expected material adverse effect |
### Conflicts
| Conflict | Quotes and locators | Downstream effect |

| Size of the August 2026 equity raise | Q2 release `page:1`: "Announcement of $2.05 Billion Equity Investment" and "a $2.05 billion equity capital investment by Oaktree Capital Management and SFS Group Capital, LLC"; Q2 10-Q `page:32` to `page:33`: "aggregate gross proceeds of $1.65 billion" and a "$400 million rights offering to Class A shareholders, with the support of Oaktree and the Ishbia Family, if needed" | Logged, not reconciled. CP-2 should model only the 1.65 billion as closed and treat the rights offering as contingent |

Affects no credit metric used here; the Q1 release figure is the one consistent with the printed total |

CP-2, then CP-5. spans.text: # CP-2 — Fundamental credit synthesis: UWM Holdings Corp (uwmc)
## Request

This credit synthesis covers UWM Holdings Corp (UWMC) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit_snapshot pathway, using filings through the Form 10-Q signed August 7, 2026. It combines the accepted financial base and the accepted business and transaction context into a fundamental credit view for the debt of UWM and Holdings LLC. It gives no relative value, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

| context | 9e4b4c779a926897468f1dfd198d157aa081551eb0aa185c7568e6564f764c9f | User run settings; not issuer evidence. Ratings, quotes and valuation inputs are empty |

Locators in brackets or tables are `page:N` of the pinned `.jsonl` text; "Q2 10-Q" is the Form 10-Q for June 30, 2026. Every CP-1 and CP-1A figure used below was re-checked against the filings while writing this answer. This answer confirms CP-1 and CP-1A and corrects neither.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| UWM's credit profile weakened in the first half of 2026: debt to equity rose to 6.13x and hedge losses cut equity. The August 2026 preferred raise of USD 1,650.0 million adds a buffer, but its terms are not supplied. | Medium | Covenant levels, the preferred stock terms and the use of proceeds are not supplied, and nothing after August 7, 2026 is covered. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Non-funding debt rose USD 1,747.5 million in six months to USD 6,040.4 million, while total equity fell USD 608.3 million to USD 985.3 million. | Leverage on equity reached 6.13x, leaving a thin loss-absorbing cushion before the August raise. | High |

| The second-quarter net loss of USD 451.9 million followed a USD 603.2 million derivative loss that Adjusted EBITDA of USD 185.9 million excludes. | Adjusted EBITDA does not capture hedge losses, so equity is directly exposed to rate moves. | Medium |

| Liquidity was USD 1,277.4 million at June 30, 2026, against USD 2,375.0 million of non-funding debt falling due in 2027. | 2027 repayments exceed current headroom, so refinancing or the August proceeds must cover them. | Medium |

| SFS Corp. controls the company, lends an undrawn subordinated USD 500.0 million revolver and received USD 261.9 million of member distributions in six months 2026. | Owner support exists on paper, but cash also flowed to the owner during a loss period. | Medium |

| The USD 1,650.0 million preferred raise carries 10.0% cash or 13.0% non-cash dividends. | It adds loss-absorbing capital and a fixed junior claim whose redemption rights are not supplied. | Medium |
### Credit view

UWM Holdings Corp is a large, agency-focused mortgage originator whose credit position weakened in the first half of 2026 but was cushioned by new capital on August 5, 2026. The strongest support is the USD 1,650.0 million preferred issue, together with scale in agency-eligible origination and a USD 5,311.5 million servicing-rights asset. The weakest point is the balance sheet: non-funding debt of USD 6,040.4 million is 6.13x total equity of USD 985.3 million, and equity fell USD 615.6 million in the second quarter, mostly from a net loss driven by derivative losses. What decides the outcome is whether the preferred terms leave creditors protected, whether the uncommitted servicing-rights lines stay available into USD 2,375.0 million of 2027 maturities, and whether hedging losses stop.
### Key findings

1. Leverage on the company's own capital measure more than doubled in six months. Non-funding debt (senior notes, servicing-rights lines, borrowings against investment securities and finance leases) rose by USD 1,747.5 million, from USD 4,292.9 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 6,040.4 million at June 30, 2026, while total equity fell by USD 608.3 million, from USD 1,593.6 million to USD 985.3 million, taking non-funding debt to equity from 2.69x to 6.13x [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]. The increase was USD 1,750.0 million of net draws on the two servicing-rights facilities, which exceeded the USD 1,237.7 million growth in the servicing-rights asset, so part of the borrowing financed operations and distributions rather than the asset. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the use of proceeds.

2. Adjusted EBITDA and net income diverged sharply because of hedging. Adjusted EBITDA for the last twelve months was USD 790.6 million, and non-funding debt was 7.64x that figure, against 6.16x at FY2025; yet the last twelve months produced a net loss of USD 105.0 million. Adjusted EBITDA excludes servicing-rights valuation changes and the result on other interest rate derivatives, which together were a net loss of USD 526.8 million over the last twelve months and USD 538.1 million in the second quarter alone. In the second quarter a derivative loss of USD 603.2 million was only partly offset by a USD 65.1 million servicing-rights valuation gain, so the hedge programme lost money net. The filings do not state the intended hedge ratio. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the hedge result.

3. Coverage of interest on non-funding debt is thinner than the headline Adjusted EBITDA suggests. Last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense on non-funding debt 2.92x, down from 3.25x at FY2025, and the second-quarter run rate is lower still at 2.14x (Adjusted EBITDA of USD 185.9 million and interest of USD 86.8 million, each annualised). These are accrual proxies because cash interest on non-funding debt is not reported separately. Category: Analyst Interpretation on CP-1 figures.

4. Liquidity is adequate for the near term but depends on lender discretion. Cash of USD 477.4 million (unrestricted) plus USD 800.0 million of undrawn lines gives USD 1,277.4 million, of which USD 300.0 million sits under uncommitted servicing-rights facilities that advance against collateral value and may be curtailed if that value falls [Q2 10-Q `page:54`, `page:55`]. The USD 500.0 million revolver is provided by the controlling holder. Scheduled non-funding repayments are USD 83.7 million in the second half of 2026 and USD 2,375.0 million in 2027 (the 2027 notes of USD 500.0 million and the Conventional servicing-rights facility of USD 1,875.0 million). Without new money, 2027 repayments would be 185.9% of current headroom. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

5. Short-dated warehouse funding is the structural exposure beneath the debt. Warehouse lines of USD 8,600.1 million fund mortgage loans of USD 9,619.1 million, only USD 900.0 million of line capacity is committed, advances are generally 97% to 98% of principal, and lines with USD 5,090.8 million advanced have expiry dates on or before May 14, 2027. Every facility, including the secured and unsecured lines, carries cross-default or cross-acceleration provisions, so a covenant breach or an unmet margin call under one could terminate all of them [Q2 10-Q `page:50`, `page:52`]. The company states compliance with all covenants at June 30, 2026, and no covenant levels are printed. Category: Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information on covenant headroom.

6. Controlling-holder structure cuts both ways. SFS Corp. holds 78.7% of Holdings LLC and about 79% of votes, receives member distributions and Tax Receivable Agreement payments (liability USD 280.0 million, accelerating on a change in control), and also subordinated its USD 500.0 million revolver to the senior notes in September 2025 and took part in the August 2026 preferred issue through a vehicle of the CEO's family [CP-1A, Ownership and control; Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Distributions and dividends paid in the first half of 2026 were USD 321.8 million against a net loss of USD 281.5 million before the dividend was suspended. Behaviour reads as mixed. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented actions.

7. The August 5, 2026 raise improves the equity position but its effect cannot yet be measured. The USD 1,650.0 million of gross proceeds has not reached any reported statement, its use of proceeds, fees and balance sheet classification are not supplied, and the contingent rights offering of USD 400 million is scheduled to expire after the cutoff. If the proceeds were retained or used to repay secured lines and were classified as equity, non-funding debt to equity would be between 2.29x and 1.67x; if the preferred is classified outside equity and proceeds repay secured lines, it would be 4.46x. These are arithmetic scenarios, not forecasts. Annual dividends at the stated rates would be USD 165.0 million in cash or USD 214.5 million non-cash. Category: Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information on terms.

8. Regulatory net worth and liquidity floors are close enough to matter. The most restrictive agency minimums are net worth of USD 743.6 million and liquidity of USD 343.9 million for UWM, against consolidated total equity of USD 985.3 million and unrestricted cash of USD 477.4 million at June 30, 2026 [Q2 10-Q `page:23`]. Consolidated equity includes non-controlling interest and is not UWM's own net worth, which is not printed, so the USD 241.7 million gap is a proxy only. A second-quarter-sized fall in equity (USD 615.6 million) would have exceeded that proxy gap before the August raise. Category: Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information on UWM-level figures.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Strengths:

- Agency-eligible, high-volume origination. About 93% of loans in the second quarter of 2026 went to Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or Ginnie Mae pools, and originations were USD 84,646.4 million for the first half of 2026, 17.4% above the first half of 2025, so most production has an agency exit and the lines turn over within a month [CP-1A, Company and operating model; CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Servicing-rights asset and earnings drivers. Servicing income rose to USD 220.5 million in the second quarter from USD 178.8 million a year earlier, and the servicing-rights asset of USD 5,311.5 million is 2.14% of USD 247.6 billion serviced; it supports secured borrowing and can be sold, with USD 801.0 million of net sale proceeds in the first half [CP-1, Earnings, cash flow and servicing drivers]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Fresh junior capital and owner participation. The August 2026 preferred and warrant issue of USD 1,650.0 million included USD 150.0 million from a vehicle of the CEO's family, the dividend was suspended, and the owner's revolver is subordinated to the senior notes [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on creditor benefit.

- Spread maturity profile on senior notes. The four note series mature in 2027, 2029, 2030 and 2031 (USD 500.0 million, 700.0 million, 800.0 million and 1,000.0 million), with none in 2028, and the 2027 notes are callable at par [CP-1, Chart data: debt maturities]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Reported covenant compliance. The company states compliance with indenture and facility covenants at June 30, 2026, and the tests that are printed for note incurrence (Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio of at least 3.0 to 1.0 or Debt-to-Equity Ratio not above 2.0 to 1.0) restrict new non-funding debt [Q2 10-Q `page:54`]. Category: Documentary Fact; the restriction's effect is Analyst Interpretation.
Weaknesses:

- High and rising leverage on thin equity. Non-funding debt to equity of 6.13x and 7.64x LTM Adjusted EBITDA; equity ex non-controlling interest is only USD 133.8 million [CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Earnings volatility and hedge losses. Net loss of USD 451.9 million in the second quarter after a USD 603.2 million derivative loss; recurring servicing-rights decay of USD 395.1 million in the first half is not added back in Adjusted EBITDA [CP-1, Adjusted EBITDA definition and reconciliation review]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Negative operating cash flow. Operating cash flow was negative USD 1,885.8 million for the first half of 2026, and negative USD 1,084.8 million after adding servicing-rights sale proceeds, against positive USD 1,919.8 million a year earlier on the same basis; secured borrowing of USD 1,750.0 million plugged the gap [CP-1, Calculations]. Category: Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on funding the gap.

- Uncommitted and short-dated funding with cross-default. Only USD 900.0 million of warehouse line capacity is committed, the servicing-rights facilities are uncommitted and collateral-based, and cross-default links all lines [Q2 10-Q `page:15`, `page:52`]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Controlling-holder claims and related-party flows. Tax Receivable Agreement liability of USD 280.0 million, member distributions of USD 261.9 million paid in the first half of 2026, and related-party payments of USD 32.9 million in FY2025 [CP-1A, Governance and sponsor behaviour; Claims outside debt in CP-1]. Category: Documentary Fact.

- Execution and legal risks. The in-house servicing transition (management targets October 2026) and class actions on broker influence, telemarketing and a vendor cyber incident; no accrual or estimate is printed [CP-1A, Timeline; Credit translations]. Category: Management Language for the timeline; Documentary Fact for the proceedings.

- Terms of the August 2026 raise are unknown. Redemption and protective rights of the Series A-1 preferred and the board rights of Oaktree could rank ahead of creditor interests in practice. The filing does not say. Category: Insufficient Information.
### Assessment, thesis and confidence
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Assessment | Fundamental credit view: weakened financial risk, supported by new junior capital; business risk is that of a scaled, agency-focused, volume-driven originator that is controlled by one holder | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Financials and credit metrics, Chart data; CP-1A Business and transaction view, Ownership and control |

| Thesis | UWM's debt is supported by agency-eligible origination, a large servicing-rights asset and fresh equity-type capital, but depends on uncommitted secured funding, volatile hedge results and thin equity until the terms and use of the August 2026 proceeds are known | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 and CP-1A as above |
| Financial risk | Leverage on equity 6.13x; non-funding debt 7.64x LTM Adjusted EBITDA; accrual coverage 2.92x | Documentary Fact | High for the figures | CP-1 Chart data: leverage, interest cover |
| Liquidity | USD 1,277.4 million, of which USD 800.0 million undrawn and USD 300.0 million uncommitted | Documentary Fact | Medium | CP-1 Chart data: liquidity |

| Confidence limit | Below High because the upstream readiness judgment for this module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and the CP-1A gaps ledger records high-severity gaps on the preferred terms and the debt agreements | Insufficient Information | n/a | CP-0, CP-1A Gaps |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Collateral-value and margin risk on funding lines | Warehouse and servicing-rights lenders revalue collateral daily or on advance rates; a decline in loan or servicing-rights value forces collateral or curtailment, and a failure can terminate lines through cross-default (Q2 10-Q `page:50`, `page:52`, `page:54`) | Liquidity could shrink quickly in a rate shock; monitoring posture should follow servicing-rights fair value and margin deposits | Critical |

| Refinancing of 2027 maturities | USD 2,375.0 million due in 2027 (2027 notes June 15 and the Conventional servicing-rights facility July 15) against USD 1,277.4 million of headroom before the raise | Requires market access, lender extension or use of the August proceeds | Material |

| Hedge programme volatility | Other interest rate derivatives lost USD 603.2 million in the second quarter against a servicing-rights valuation gain of USD 65.1 million, and a notional of USD 12,805.0 million remained at June 30, 2026; the hedge intent and remaining exposure are not described in detail | Equity erosion that Adjusted EBITDA does not show; a repeat of the second quarter's equity fall would take consolidated equity (985.3 less 615.6 = 369.7) below the agency net worth minimum proxy before the August raise | Material |

| Thin equity and agency floors | Consolidated equity of USD 985.3 million against UWM net worth minimum of USD 743.6 million | Breach consequences include termination of agency selling and servicing rights; UWM-level figures not printed | Material |

| Controlling holder interests | Distributions, Tax Receivable Agreement payments (accelerating on change in control) and related-party arrangements | Cash can leave ahead of creditors; subordinated revolver and dividend suspension partly offset | Material |

| Preferred stock terms | Cumulative 10.0% cash or 13.0% non-cash dividends and unspecified redemption rights | A redemption claim or governance rights could constrain debt service or refinancing; terms unknown | Material |

| Servicing transition and conduct risk | In-house servicing launch, one sub-servicer, class actions and a vendor incident | Operational and legal cost; servicing-rights value could be affected | Minor |
| Cash interest not reported separately | Coverage is on an accrual basis | Coverage may differ in cash terms | Minor |
### What would change the view

- Improvement: the certificate of designation shows no holder redemption right ahead of debt maturities; use of proceeds repays secured lines; hedge losses stop and equity rebuilds; the 2027 notes and the Conventional facility are extended; uncommitted capacity is replaced by committed lines.

- Deterioration: further derivative losses; servicing-rights fair value falls and lenders curtail advances; a warehouse line is not renewed on or after its expiry; the rights offering fails or the preferred carries a near-term redemption right; distributions to the controlling holder resume while equity is thin.
## Calculations
All inputs are from the cited handoffs or filings. Amounts are USD millions unless stated.
### Run-rate and coverage

CLEARANCE DECISION: Pass with Remediation. Critical Issues: 0. Material Issues: 2. Minor Issues: 9. Committee Use: Restricted.

No finding changes a reported figure or the direction of the credit view, so none is Critical. Two Material findings (CP5-001 and CP5-002) are legal-meaning overreaches in the business-context and synthesis handoffs that must be disclosed or removed before committee use. - CP-1A (Credit translations, Hybrid capital) and CP-2 (Reader summary, Weaknesses): the descriptions of the preferred as a junior claim to debt, and of its rights as possibly ranking ahead of creditor interests, are withdrawn. - CP-1 (chart tables): the interest cover cells are accrual-based, the undrawn column includes uncommitted lines, and "total debt" in the leverage chart is non-funding debt.
